items.title: A report, an agentless report, a prohibition

states.label: The doer named
states.sm: Sā tatala e le teine le pusa.
states.note: The doer is marked and the box stands bare.

states.label: The doer absent
states.note: The doer is removed and nothing replaces it.

states.label: The action forbidden
states.sm: ʻAua le tatala=ina le pusa lenā.
states.note: Forbidding with *ʻaua le* requires the long form.

items.caption: Review three uses of the same verb. The last sentence follows a firm command rule, while the ordinary report uses the short form as its default.

items.title: Read the relationship between clauses

items.sm: ʻUa alu le tama ʻona ʻua sau le teine.
items.en: The boy went because the girl came.
items.why: The because-word opens a clause with its own tense particle.

items.sm: ʻUa mālamalama le teine ʻauā ʻua tautala le tama.
items.en: The girl understands because the boy has spoken.
items.why: The second clause gives the reason for the first.

items.sm: Sā alu le tama e ʻaumai le niu.
items.en: The boy went to bring the coconut.
items.why: The clause headed by *e* tells what the going was for.

items.sm: ʻĀfai e timu taeao, e lē alu le malaga.
items.en: If it rains tomorrow, the trip will not go.
items.why: The first clause says what has to be true before the main clause follows.

items.intro: Choose what the added clause contributes, using the patterns already learned.
